messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency breach in dedicated pool helio-eu-1 (eu-central). Metric: serving.latency.p99 >= 2.4s for 3m. Paging oncall-asia. https://redwood.internal/alerts/2350001234 :rotating_light:
oncall-asia: I'm on it, waking up the war room. grabbing dashboards now.
sre-jamie: I can join in 2m, saw similar flaps earlier in ap-southeast when Helio increased concurrent synth requests.
sre-lee: pulling pool metrics + tenant breakdown. first glance: Helio tenant burst from 300->1600 concurrent requests at ~2350001200, KV cache miss rate spiked to 92%.
eng-runtime: we had a canary roll three hours ago for LRU cache change in runtime (PR #4821). can confirm TTL tweak was applied to dedicated pools.
pm-ana: customer Helio (enterprise VPC + dedicated) just pinged their SRE asking if we're seeing slowness. keep them in the loop.
customer-helio-sre: we're seeing timeouts from our side too, some calls > 5s. This is impacting checkout flows for EU customers. Any ETA?
sre-jamie: short assessment: p95 also elevated ~800ms -> 1.2s. p99 shoots to 2.5-5s. Impacting synchronous calls. probable cause: cache thrash after TTL reduction + tenant burst.
eng-runtime: confirm: the canary changed metadata cache TTL from 60s -> 5s for LRU eviction tuning. That increases KV lookups. We didn't pin config to dedicated pools; canary rolled too broadly. my bad.
infra-ops: starting emergency mitigation steps: 1) throttle tenant concurrency at ingress for Helio 2) route Helio traffic to warm-spare pool in ap-southeast as temporary relief 3) rollback canary config on helio-eu-1.
sre-lee: I'll run commands to snapshot current pods and scale warm spare.
devops-bot: Runbook link: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/tenant-latency-mitigation. Steps 2-5 recommended.
eng-runtime: hold on before routing cross-region — need to confirm data compliance. Helio requested EU-only. we can failover to helio-eu-2 (warm spare) not ap-southeast.
infra-ops: ack, switching to helio-eu-2. executing scale up.
eng-runtime: command to add nodes to dedicated pool:
```
redwoodctl pool scale --pool helio-eu-2 --nodes 6 --profile dedicated
```
started that now.
sre-jamie: applying ingress throttle for Helio tenant at edge-proxy: reduce concurrency to 400 for 10m
```
edgectl set-tenant-quota --tenant helio --concurrency 400 --duration 10m
```
applied. monitoring.
customer-helio-sre: thanks, we can temporarily reduce client-side concurrency as well while you stabilize. we'll throttle to 300 on our end.
eng-runtime: rolling back runtime cache TTL for dedicated pools to 60s. patch command:
```
kubectl -n runtime patch configmap runtime-cache-config -p '{"data":{"kv_ttl_seconds":"60"}}'
```
watching for propagation.
sre-lee: after rollback, KV miss rate dropping from 92% -> 26% within 90s. p99 dropped from 2.6s -> 780ms.
pm-ana: communicating to Helio account team: "we've identified a bad canary config change affecting dedicated pools; we've rolled it back and applied ingress throttles and warm-spare scaling. Monitoring for stabilization."
customer-helio-sre: appreciate the fast response. please keep us posted on SLO recovery and any root cause timeline.
infra-ops: warm-spare scale finished, health checks passing on helio-eu-2.
sre-jamie: note: there are 2 heavy background jobs from Helio running reports which correlate with the burst window. recommend we ask customer to reschedule non-critical batch jobs to off-peak.
customer-helio-sre: yes, we see that — we paused the largest report and that reduced pressure. thanks.
eng-runtime: deploying a targeted patch to ensure canary config doesn't apply to dedicated pools unless flagged:
```
# runtime config guard
if pool.type == "dedicated" and config.change.origin == "canary":
  reject_change()
```
will ship the guard now.
sre-lee: once guard is live, propose we do a controlled replay to validate no regressions in staging before re-enabling TTL change.
oncall-asia: handing off to night oncall (sre-lee) at 2350001300. I'll drop a summary in the incident ticket.
sre-lee: taking over. summary for handoff: root cause = canary TTL regression applied to dedicated pools causing KV cache thrash under tenant burst. mitigations = rollback TTL, ingress throttle, warm-spare scaling, customer throttling. current state = p99 ~ 600-800ms, KV miss ~22%, helio-eu-2 healthy.
pm-ana: opening post-incident ticket and scheduling RCA meeting with eng-runtime, infra, and Helio reps. tentative time: 2350006000 (4h).
customer-helio-sre: we'll join RCA. want confirm if any request logs were lost during the window.
sre-jamie: no request logs dropped, just higher latency and some downstream timeouts. audit logs available in S3: s3://redwood-logs/helio/2350001234/*.
infra-ops: closing immediate mitigation tasks in checklist. leaving throttle for 30m then re-evaluate.
sre-lee: monitoring for 15m then plan to remove ingress throttle if stable. p99 trending down.
eng-runtime: guard patch deployed to canary gate. will follow up with tests.
devops-bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2350001234. Runbook steps executed: throttle, rollback, scale warm-spare, customer throttle.
oncall-asia: resolved from my side, handing to lee. great team response. :clap:
sre-lee: marking war room inactive at 2350001399, will update ticket with final notes and schedule RCA.
customer-helio-sre: service looking stable from our side, thanks for quick fix. we'll coordinate on long-term isolation controls.
eng-runtime: action items: 1) add canary guard for dedicated pools (done) 2) add automated tenant-throttle trigger in runtime when KV miss > 60% and p99>2s 3) improved preflight checks for config changes.
pm-ana: I'll follow up with account team and customer comms.
sre-jamie: closing thread, keeping monitoring on until 2350001499.
